page.layout: Top centre: two round engraved medallions side by side, the left with the legend SER. GALBA IMP. SAES AVG., the right with LEPIDA GALBAE IMP VXOR. Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs (the first a biography of Galba, the second about Lepida). No margin notes, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.l: SER. GALBA IMP. SAES [?] AVG.
LEPIDA GALBAE IMP VXOR.
SERGIVS Sulpitius Galba, Romæ post Neronē imperat
anno mundi 4030. à Christo nato 68. Hic nullo gradu Cæsa-
res contingebat, nam horum familia, siue progenies in Nero-
nē defecerat: nobilissimus tamen erat, magnáq; & vetere pro-
sapia. Antequàm imperaret mula fertur peperisse. Hic cùm
Prætor esset, elephantos funambulos edidit ludis Floralibus.
Maiore ab initio fauore quàm læto successu, septimestre impe-
rium tenuit annos natus circiter 80. priuata eius vita insignis
fuerat militaribus & ciuilibus rebus. Tandem auarum, sæuum,
pigrum se præstitit: atque inuisus omnibus, in medio foro, insi-
diis Othonis iugulatur: nam cùm subinde iactaret se legere
militem, uon emere consuesse, eo nomine omnes milites exa-
cerbauit. Sed maximè fremebat superioris Germaniæ exerci-
tus fraudari se præmiis: quare statim legationem ad prætoria-
nos cum mandatis destinant: displicere inquiunt Imperato-
rem in Hispania factum, eligerent ipsi quem cuncti exercitus
probarent. Quamobrem ascitus Otho eum trucidari curauit.
Vide Sueto.in Galba, Eutro.lib.7. Bap.Egna.lib.1.
LEPIDA vxor fuit Galbæ Imperatoris, qua amissa, duo-
búsque ex ea filiis, remansit in cœlibatu: neque solicitari vlla
conditione amplius potuit, ne Agrippinæ quidem matris Ne-
ronis, viduatæ morte Domitij Aenobarbi, quæ maritum quoq;
adhuc, necdum cœlibem Galbam, adeò omnibus solicitauerat
modis, vt in conuentu matronarum correpta iurgio, atq; etiam
manu pullata sit à matre Lepidæ. Sueto.in Gal.

page.notes: Coin legends are read from the engraving; "SAES" on the left medallion is doubtful. "uon" in "uon emere" is printed as such (probably for non) and is left as printed. "consuesse" is read from a worn "confuesse"; check against the scan. Paragraph 2 is set in a heavier face than paragraph 1, but no italics are used. The small mark near the lower margin is a stain and not transcribed.
